rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.evidence_storage`. I judged this from the supplied test text alone and did not request implementation source.

- **Absence and load failure.**
  - `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/contracts.rs#fn[criteria_keep_typed_answers_and_persist_only_when_requested]` asserts `Ok(None)` before the first save. It also asserts `Ok(None)` after `verify`, because execution alone does not save.
  - `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/storage.rs#fn[consumer_delegates_evidence_storage_using_only_the_requested_nodes_path]` asserts `Ok(None)` for an absent node. It then writes corrupt bytes and asserts `Err(FileStorageError::Json(_))`, which covers "Err means loading failed".
  - `src/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[domain_storage_round_trips_each_review_kind_and_preserves_records_on_errors]` checks absence and failure paths for the domain storage.
- **Round trip and replacement of only this pair's record.**
  - The contracts test stores a record, loads it, and compares output, source, criterion, revision and dependencies.
  - It then runs `verify` on a replacement answer for the same criterion without saving. The saved record stays unchanged, so only an explicit `store_evidence` replaces it.
  - `src/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[domain_storage_round_trips_each_review_kind_and_preserves_records_on_errors]` round-trips a record with revision, dependencies and output. Failed stores leave the on-disk bytes unchanged.
- **Key preserves both parts.** `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/storage.rs#fn[source_and_criterion_boundaries_preserve_independent_records]` uses the exact pair from the text, source `["a"]` with criterion `["b","c"]` against source `["a","b"]` with criterion `["c"]`. It also uses empty, empty-string and control-character segments. Each pair is absent before its save. After all pairs are stored, each loads back its own distinct output.
- **Independent criteria and no new key on revision change.**
  - The contracts test saves `behavior`, `structure` and `text` criteria of the same source. Each loads independently.
  - `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/contracts.rs#fn[concurrent_same_criterion_executions_keep_complete_independent_records]` stores two records with different revisions for one criterion. It asserts `state.records.len() == 1`, so a revision change replaces the record instead of creating another key.
- **Loads see an old or new complete record, or absence before the first save.** `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/storage.rs#fn[concurrent_readers_only_observe_complete_records_from_competing_writes]` has two writers storing 8 KiB records repeatedly while a reader loads continuously.
  - Every successful load must be a complete record from A or B, or the initial record. The output id, padding length, revision and dependencies must all agree.
  - The test also asserts that no stray files are left in the directory.
- **Competing saves leave one complete record from one save.** The contracts concurrent test saves two records concurrently. It asserts that the single surviving record's revision and dependencies match its own output, in either order. This matches the "no ordering guaranteed" clause.
- **Not testable.** "Requires neither filesystem paths nor global listing" is an interface property. The contracts tests use a non-filesystem `Application` domain and a `Node(u32)` id, which supports it.

I found no unchecked obligation and no assertion that contradicts the text.

text: /// Ok(None) means absent; Err means loading failed.
/// Atomically replace only this source/criterion pair's complete record.
The validator passes the source identity and criterion path to both methods. The
key preserves both parts: source paths `["a"]` and `["a", "b"]` with criteria
`["b", "c"]` and `["c"]` identify different records, even though flattening each
pair would produce the same segments.
Different criteria of a source have independent records. A revision change
invalidates the same criterion's record rather than creating another key.
The interface requires neither filesystem paths nor global evidence listing.
Successful loads observe either an old or new complete record, or absence
before the first save. Successful competing saves leave one complete record;
its revision, dependencies, and output all belong to that save. No ordering
